name: Haggai
author: Haggai was a prophet, someone called to speak God's messages to the people, who lived in Jerusalem after the Jews returned from exile in Babylon. We know almost nothing about his family or background; outside this book he appears only briefly in the book of Ezra, alongside the prophet Zechariah. Traditionally Haggai is seen as the author of his own messages, though because the book speaks of him in the third person, many scholars think a follower or editor gathered and arranged his words soon after he spoke them.
audience: Haggai first spoke to the small community of Jews who had come back to Jerusalem and the surrounding land of Judah, along with their leaders, Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest (the chief priest). Nearly twenty years earlier they had begun rebuilding God's temple, but the work had stalled amid opposition from neighbours, poor harvests and the struggle to rebuild their own homes and lives.
era: Haggai's messages are dated to 520 BC, in the second year of Darius I, king of the vast Persian Empire, who had seized the throne after a period of upheaval and revolts. Persia had conquered Babylon in 539 BC, and its king Cyrus allowed exiled Jews to return home and rebuild the temple that the Babylonians had destroyed in 586 BC. Judah was now a small, poor province within the Persian Empire, and Jerusalem still lay largely in ruins. The rebuilt temple was finished around 516 BC.

notes.1:1: Dated to the first day of the sixth month in Darius's second year, around late August 520 BC, and addressed to Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest.
notes.1:12: Work on the temple resumed on the twenty-fourth day of that same month, around September 520 BC, just over three weeks after Haggai's first message.
notes.2:1: Dated to the twenty-first day of the seventh month, around October 520 BC, the last day of the Feast of Tabernacles, a week-long harvest festival when people lived in shelters.
notes.2:10: Dated to the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, around December 520 BC, three months after rebuilding resumed, and includes questions put to the priests about rules of ritual cleanness.
notes.2:20: Given on the same December day as the previous message and addressed to Zerubbabel alone, a grandson of King Jehoiachin and so a descendant of King David.

flags.problem: 'Nearly twenty years earlier' overstates the gap. The temple foundations were laid around 537–536 BC, about sixteen or seventeen years before Haggai spoke in 520 BC.
flags.suggestion: Change to 'About sixteen years earlier' or 'Some years earlier'.

flags.problem: The date for resumed work (the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month) comes from 1:15, not 1:12. A reader looking at 1:12 will not find it there.
flags.suggestion: Start the note at 1:14 or 1:15, or say the date is given a few verses later at the end of the chapter.

flags.problem: 'Rules of ritual cleanness' may confuse an ordinary reader, and the rules ask for such terms to be explained.
flags.suggestion: Add a short gloss, e.g. 'rules about ritual cleanness (whether a person or thing was fit to take part in worship)'.
